k: Singing glass grows deep in the Glass Caverns, where the old Lantern-light soaked into the sand for a thousand years.
src: 'Singing glass grows deep in the Glass Caverns, where the old Lantern-light soaked into the sand for a thousand years.'

k: It hums to sunlight. And to music, they say — if you've got the right note. Old Keeper's trick. Nobody's got the right note anymore.
src: 'It hums to sunlight. And to music, they say — if you\'ve got the right note. Old Keeper\'s trick. Nobody\'s got the right note anymore.'

k: Glass is just sand that's been through something.
src: 'Glass is just sand that\'s been through something.'

k: Like people. Hotter the fire, clearer the glass. That's my philosophy, and also my sales pitch.
src: 'Like people. Hotter the fire, clearer the glass. That\'s my philosophy, and also my sales pitch.'

k: Not a raider in sight since you ran off the Jackal. My men are bored. Bored is beautiful.
src: 'Not a raider in sight since you ran off the Jackal. My men are bored. Bored is beautiful.'

k: Sarn ran? The Jackal himself? Ha! The caravans will drink to you for a month.
src: 'Sarn ran? The Jackal himself? Ha! The caravans will drink to you for a month.'

k: The council's purse, as promised. Don't spend it all in the inn. Do spend some of it in the inn. My cousin runs it.
src: 'The council\'s purse, as promised. Don\'t spend it all in the inn. Do spend some of it in the inn. My cousin runs it.'

k: Sarn's camp is in the Sunscar's south-east flats, past the glass. Red tents. Mind his slingers — they aim for the eyes.
src: 'Sarn\'s camp is in the Sunscar\'s south-east flats, past the glass. Red tents. Mind his slingers — they aim for the eyes.'

k: Pilgrims with swords. Good. I've a job, if you want it.
src: 'Pilgrims with swords. Good. I\'ve a job, if you want it.'

k: Sarn the Jackal: raider-king of the southern dunes. Camp's in the Sunscar's south-east flats. He takes a tithe from every caravan — water, coin, sometimes people.
src: 'Sarn the Jackal: raider-king of the southern dunes. Camp\'s in the Sunscar\'s south-east flats. He takes a tithe from every caravan — water, coin, sometimes people.'

k: My men can't touch him; they're needed on the walls. The town council has put up two thousand gold to see him gone.
src: 'My men can\'t touch him; they\'re needed on the walls. The town council has put up two thousand gold to see him gone.'

k: The Jackal's Tithe
src: 'The Jackal\'s Tithe'

k: Captain Idris will pay 2,000 gold to see Sarn the Jackal driven from his camp in the south-east of the Sunscar (west of Saltglass).
src: 'Captain Idris will pay 2,000 gold to see Sarn the Jackal driven from his camp in the south-east of the Sunscar (west of Saltglass).'

k: Papa's caravan is late. Mama says he's just slow.
src: 'Papa\'s caravan is late. Mama says he\'s just slow.'

k: Papa's not slow. Papa's the fastest scout on the whole salt road. So he's not late. He's just... not here yet.
src: 'Papa\'s not slow. Papa\'s the fastest scout on the whole salt road. So he\'s not late. He\'s just... not here yet.'

k: ...How long you been waiting?
src: '...How long you been waiting?'

k: Nine days. I bring my lunch.
src: 'Nine days. I bring my lunch.'

k: If you see Papa, tell him I'm waiting at the gate. He'll know which one. It's this one.
src: 'If you see Papa, tell him I\'m waiting at the gate. He\'ll know which one. It\'s this one.'

k: He's ELEVEN?! He got Kindled at ELEVEN?!
src: 'He\'s ELEVEN?! He got Kindled at ELEVEN?!'

k: I've been waiting fifteen years and eleven months! I've been _good!_
src: 'I\'ve been waiting fifteen years and eleven months! I\'ve been _good!_'

k: ...What did he get? Rogue? Okay. Okay, I feel a little better.
src: '...What did he get? Rogue? Okay. Okay, I feel a little better.'

k: Fifteen years and eleven months. ELEVEN MONTHS. And they won't let me stand in the light for thirty more days.
src: 'Fifteen years and eleven months. ELEVEN MONTHS. And they won\'t let me stand in the light for thirty more days.'

k: What if it changes its mind? What if the light was going to say Arcanist and in thirty days it says Accountant?
src: 'What if it changes its mind? What if the light was going to say Arcanist and in thirty days it says Accountant?'

k: The Queen is dead? Truly? ...My brother's caravan went into that dark eleven years ago.
src: 'The Queen is dead? Truly? ...My brother\'s caravan went into that dark eleven years ago.'

k: Three thousand gold, as I promised. And this — it was his. He'd have wanted it worn by someone braver than a caravan master.
src: 'Three thousand gold, as I promised. And this — it was his. He\'d have wanted it worn by someone braver than a caravan master.'

k: Caravans north leave when the Keeper says the stars are right. She hasn't said.
src: 'Caravans north leave when the Keeper says the stars are right. She hasn\'t said.'

k: Go and see her. Everybody goes and sees her. Then they come back here looking thoughtful and pay me.
src: 'Go and see her. Everybody goes and sees her. Then they come back here looking thoughtful and pay me.'

k: Tamsin says I owe her? I owe her my eyes, my caravan, and my second wife. Fine. North it is, whenever you're ready.
src: 'Tamsin says I owe her? I owe her my eyes, my caravan, and my second wife. Fine. North it is, whenever you\'re ready.'

k: One more thing, since you look like the sort who goes into caves. The Glass Caverns, out the east gate — there's a Queen down there.
src: 'One more thing, since you look like the sort who goes into caves. The Glass Caverns, out the east gate — there\'s a Queen down there.'

k: A sand wyrm, old as sin and twice as hungry. She ate my brother's caravan. Ate the Kessel caravan nine days ago, I'd wager. Kill her, and I'll pay three thousand gold.
src: 'A sand wyrm, old as sin and twice as hungry. She ate my brother\'s caravan. Ate the Kessel caravan nine days ago, I\'d wager. Kill her, and I\'ll pay three thousand gold.'

k: Queen of the Glass
src: 'Queen of the Glass'

k: Caravan Master Oyelaran will pay 3,000 gold for the death of the Sand Wyrm Queen, deep in the Glass Caverns beyond Saltglass's east gate.
src: 'Caravan Master Oyelaran will pay 3,000 gold for the death of the Sand Wyrm Queen, deep in the Glass Caverns beyond Saltglass\'s east gate.'

k: Travel north to the Greyspine
src: 'Travel north to the Greyspine'

k: Nine days north by caravan. (You can return to Saltglass later.)
src: 'Nine days north by caravan. (You can return to Saltglass later.)'

k: The wagons will wait. The wagons always wait. It's the camels that get impatient.
src: 'The wagons will wait. The wagons always wait. It\'s the camels that get impatient.'

k: Nine days north by caravan: across the flats, through the scrublands, up into country where the air turns thin and the wind tastes of iron.
src: 'Nine days north by caravan: across the flats, through the scrublands, up into country where the air turns thin and the wind tastes of iron.'

k: At the foot of the Greyspine, Oyelaran's wagons turn back.
src: 'At the foot of the Greyspine, Oyelaran\'s wagons turn back.'

k: "This is as far as wheels go," he says. "The monastery's a day's climb. Walk softly. The mountain listens."
src: '"This is as far as wheels go," he says. "The monastery\'s a day\'s climb. Walk softly. The mountain listens."'

k: Inside, the light comes from everywhere at once — from the lamp above, from the glass walls, from the glass floor — and none of it casts a shadow.
src: 'Inside, the light comes from everywhere at once — from the lamp above, from the glass walls, from the glass floor — and none of it casts a shadow.'

k: A woman sits on the steps of the dais with a cane across her knees. Her eyes are the milky white of saltglass. She is smiling at the door before it opens.
src: 'A woman sits on the steps of the dais with a cane across her knees. Her eyes are the milky white of saltglass. She is smiling at the door before it opens.'

k: Six of you. No — five, and one who walks like a cat that's been told off.
src: 'Six of you. No — five, and one who walks like a cat that\'s been told off.'

k: Oi!
src: 'Oi!'

k: A big one who walks like he's apologizing to the floor.
src: 'A big one who walks like he\'s apologizing to the floor.'

k: A careful one who counts her steps. A man already looking for the back door.
src: 'A careful one who counts her steps. A man already looking for the back door.'

k: In my defense, there usually is one.
src: 'In my defense, there usually is one.'

k: And one who doesn't walk quite the way the rest of you do. You... drift. Like a song somebody's humming.
src: 'And one who doesn\'t walk quite the way the rest of you do. You... drift. Like a song somebody\'s humming.'

k: I walk. I have feet.
src: 'I walk. I have feet.'

k: So you do, sweetling. So you do.
src: 'So you do, sweetling. So you do.'

k: And the one in front walks like someone leaving. Come here, Wren Halloway.
src: 'And the one in front walks like someone leaving. Come here, Wren Halloway.'

k: How do you know my—
src: 'How do you know my—'

k: Ysolde's girl. I knew your grandmother's step, and your mother's. You have both. Your mother hated being told that.
src: 'Ysolde\'s girl. I knew your grandmother\'s step, and your mother\'s. You have both. Your mother hated being told that.'

k: ...She still does.
src: '...She still does.'

k: Good. Now. What has Cassian sent me?
src: 'Good. Now. What has Cassian sent me?'

k: Wren opens the case. Tamsin's fingers find a fork without searching, the way you find the latch of your own door in the dark.
src: 'Wren opens the case. Tamsin\'s fingers find a fork without searching, the way you find the latch of your own door in the dark.'

k: She strikes it once against her cane and holds it to her ear. The note is pure and thin, and it goes on much longer than it should.
src: 'She strikes it once against her cane and holds it to her ear. The note is pure and thin, and it goes on much longer than it should.'

k: Tamsin's smile goes away.
src: 'Tamsin\'s smile goes away.'

k: ...It sings a note I almost know.
src: '...It sings a note I almost know.'

k: Is something wrong with it?
src: 'Is something wrong with it?'

k: Like a word in a language I used to speak. Like a name I heard in a dream and lost on waking.
src: 'Like a word in a language I used to speak. Like a name I heard in a dream and lost on waking.'

k: I've listened to the Dawnsong every morning for fifty-one years, child. I know every note of it the way you know your mother's voice. This is one of them. And it is not.
src: 'I\'ve listened to the Dawnsong every morning for fifty-one years, child. I know every note of it the way you know your mother\'s voice. This is one of them. And it is not.'

k: The Hierophant had them made in the Cathedral. To harmonize the Lanterns, against the Gloam—
src: 'The Hierophant had them made in the Cathedral. To harmonize the Lanterns, against the Gloam—'

k: I know what he said. Cassian always says exactly the right thing.
src: 'I know what he said. Cassian always says exactly the right thing.'

k: I've known him since he was a boy who couldn't sleep unless a lamp was burning. I trust him to be exactly who he is.
src: 'I\'ve known him since he was a boy who couldn\'t sleep unless a lamp was burning. I trust him to be exactly who he is.'

k: That is what worries me.
src: 'That is what worries me.'

k: She lays the fork back in its velvet, gently, like something that might bite.
src: 'She lays the fork back in its velvet, gently, like something that might bite.'

k: Take it to Halvard at Frosthollow, north in the Greyspine. He has forgotten more about the Dawnsong than the Choir ever knew. If Halvard says it is true, I will set it in my light with my own hands.
src: 'Take it to Halvard at Frosthollow, north in the Greyspine. He has forgotten more about the Dawnsong than the Choir ever knew. If Halvard says it is true, I will set it in my light with my own hands.'

k: And if he says it isn't?
src: 'And if he says it isn\'t?'

k: Then you will have learned something about the world, Wren Halloway. That's what sixteen is for.
src: 'Then you will have learned something about the world, Wren Halloway. That\'s what sixteen is for.'

k: Pip has wandered up the dais steps, very casually, toward the little silver bell on Tamsin's belt.
src: 'Pip has wandered up the dais steps, very casually, toward the little silver bell on Tamsin\'s belt.'

k: Tamsin's hand closes on his wrist without looking.
src: 'Tamsin\'s hand closes on his wrist without looking.'

k: And you, little cat.
src: 'And you, little cat.'
